# Summary

In this study, we analyzed data within residents and directors, then compared the groups' answer selections, informing the difference that various factors can have on a resident's knowledge and experience in their program, and if the directors have a different perception of what residents face during residency. Out of 10 tests within the residents group, we found 4 to be significant controlling the FDR at 0.05. When cross-comparing the groups on each common question, 4 of the 23 test were found to be significant after adjusting for multiple hypothesis testing.  FDR was controlled via the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure at the 0.05 rate.  All tests results are reported in the significant findings section, and their significance before and after adjustment is presented.

# Methods

We conducted Fisher tests due to low expected cell counts in contingency tables. p-values were computed via simulation to reduce computational time.  For cross referencing 2x11x12, we performed a logistic regression model to predict the probability of answering "Yes" on Q2 with Q11 and Q12 as predictor variables.  

For questions that had multiple parts, we had to split them into individual questions (e.g. 11a, 11b, 11c...) to see if there were specific responses that were influenced by the grouping variable in question, which was the role (being a resident/director) in the case of cross-comparison, or information like program, experience, etc.

To visualize differences, we created side-by-side bar charts which plot the distribution of question responses versus the grouping variable. For the specific 2x11x12 question, a visualization of the regression model was created to show the probability of a resident continuing in their program after finishing residency. For resident/director comparison, side-by-side plots of the residents' response to a question versus the directors' are shown. Noticeable/interesting plots and findings were placed in the "significant findings" section. All plots, significant or not, along with the full code for generating this report can be found in the appendix.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
validation <- function(question1, question2, data){
  df <- data %>%
    transmute(
      response1 = .data[[question1]],
      response2 = .data[[question2]]
    ) %>%
    drop_na()
  
  comparison_res <- df %>%
    group_by(response1, response2) %>%
    summarize(counts = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(response2) %>%
    mutate(percent = counts / sum(counts) * 100) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  table_comparison <- table(df$response2, df$response1)
  #table_hours
  test <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(table_comparison))
  
  if (mean(test$expected <= 5) < 0.8 | any(test$expected < 1)){
    fish_test <- fisher.test(table_comparison, simulate.p.value = TRUE)
    if (fish_test$p.value <= 0.05){
      significant <- TRUE
    }
    else {
      significant <- FALSE
    }
    return(c("question1", "question2", round(fish_test$p.value, digits = 4), significant, "fisher"))
  }
  else{
    if (test$p.value <= 0.05){
      significant <- TRUE
    }
    else {
      significant <- FALSE
    }
  }
  return(c("question1", "question2", round(test$p.value, digits = 4), significant, "chisq"))
}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
res_results <- data.frame(
  Question1 = character(),
  Question2 = character(),
  P_value = numeric(),
  Significant = logical(), 
  Test = character()
)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(question_dic_res))) {

  res_results[i, ] <- validation(
    question1 = question_dic_res$question1s[i],
    question2 = question_dic_res$question2s[i],
    data = i_res_coalesced
  )
}

res_results <- res_results %>%
  mutate(
    Adj_P = round(p.adjust(P_value, method = "BH"), digits = 4),
    Sig_Adj = Adj_P <= 0.05,
    Question1 = question_dic_res$question1s, 
    Question2 = question_dic_res$question2s
  ) %>% 
  arrange(Adj_P)

```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
stack_bar <- function(q_reference, q_group, data){
  bar_df <- data %>%
    group_by(.data[[q_reference]], .data[[q_group]]) %>%
    summarize(counts = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    drop_na() %>%
    group_by(.data[[q_group]]) %>%
    mutate(percent = counts / sum(counts) * 100) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  p <- ggplot(bar_df, aes(x = .data[[q_reference]], y = percent, fill = .data[[q_reference]])) +
    geom_col() +
    facet_wrap(vars(.data[[q_group]])) +
    labs(
      title = paste(q_reference, "vs", q_group, sep = " "),
      x = NULL,
      y = "Percent of responses"
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
    )
  return(p)
}
```

# Significant Findings

## Residents Significance

The following question combinations were found significant after correcting for multiple hypothesis testing:

 - Q2 vs Q8a
 - Q2 vs Q8b
 - Q2 vs Q8c
 - Q2 vs Q8d
 

The levels of Question 8a-d are: Feel prepared to:

 a\)  provide appropriate care for a patient with a cleft or craniofacial...

 b\) identify and collaborate with the appropriate specialists as part of a cleft...

 c\) manage pre-surgical and post-surgical dental care for patients with cleft or...

 d\) manage behavioral and psychosocial considerations when providing care to patients...

```{r, echo = FALSE}
sig_res_plots <- plots_res[c(5, 6, 7, 8)]
walk(sig_res_plots, print)
```

## Q2x11x12: Association with cleft center/desire to be involved in cleft care post-residency/type of institution

For this analysis, we performed a logistic regression model to predict Yes/No in question 2 as a function of Q11 and Q12.  We see from this model summary in Table 1 that we have one parameter that is significant (being at a hospital-based program).  This means that relative to the baseline, which is a Combination (University + Hospital), someone in a Hospital based program is much less likely to answer Yes to Question 2. The coefficient estimate for hospital-based programs is -1.635, which means that if a resident is in a hospital-based program, the odds of them wanting to continue into cleft care are 5.13 (95% CI: `r round(1/exp(confint(cleft_glm))[3,c(2,1)],2)`) times lower relative to the odds of a resident in a hybrid program.  (Note: Odds ratio is computed as follows: $e^{1.635} =  5.129$)

```{r, echo = FALSE}
library(tinytable)
library(modelsummary)
modelsummary(models = list(cleft_glm),
             stars = T,
             gof_omit = ".",
  shape = term ~ model + statistic,
  coef_map = c("(Intercept)" = "Intercept",
               "cleft_centerYes"  = "Cleft Center (Yes)" ,
            "programHospital-based" = "Program (Hospital Based)",
              "programUniversity" =  "Program (University)"
                 ), 
  title = "Logistic Regression Summary: Predicting Desired Involvement in Cleft Care"
             ) %>% style_tt(
    align = "c",
    fontsize = 0.9,
    bootstrap_class = "table caption-top"
  )

```

    - a\) provide appropriate care for a patient with a cleft or craniofacial...
    - c\) manage pre-surgical and post-surgical dental care for patients with cleft or...
